properties.decision:
RECORDED AS THE SHAPE QUESTION UNDER `req:a-session-chooses-its-design`. Anthony 2026-08-05 stated a preference — "I like this approach of just pointing .mcp.json at the graph_id" — which is a lean toward (a), not a settlement, because the trade-off below was not in front of him when he said it.

(a) EDIT `.mcp.json` AND RECONNECT. WORKS TODAY WITH ZERO CODE: `--graph-path` is an ordinary argument and accepts an absolute path, so any project's server can be pointed at any store right now. The agent can make the edit — Anthony's own point, "an agent within a session can usually change files". Counter: it costs a `/mcp` reconnect, and reconnecting is a step this project has already recorded as the one an autonomous agent CANNOT take ([BL-123]). So the cheap option's cost falls exactly on the case reflow2 most wants to serve.

(b) A GRAPH REFERENCE CARRIED PER CALL (the field report's 2a). No reconnect; a session could even read one design and write another. Counter, and it is the strong one: this project already faced the identical shape for seats and went the other way — `dec:stateless-seat-handle` REFUSES a claim without a seat rather than guessing one, because a handle that changes under you is worse than one you must supply. A defaulted graph reference is that hazard with worse consequences: getting a seat wrong misattributes a claim, getting a graph wrong WRITES TO THE WRONG DESIGN, which is the very accident this whole thread began with.

⭐ THE RULE THAT SHOULD SURVIVE WHICHEVER IS CHOSEN, and it is the contribution rather than the choice: DEFAULT WHEN EXACTLY ONE DESIGN IS REACHABLE; REFUSE AND LIST THEM WHEN SEVERAL ARE. That is `dec:no-design-here-never-looked` option (a) and this node's option (b) doing one job at two moments — discovery before creating, refusal before writing. A design chosen by silence is how three graphs appeared on one repo.

THE DISCOVERY HALF, WHICH BOTH OPTIONS NEED AND NEITHER PROVIDES. Anthony asked for "a reflow2 tool to simply return all graph_ids". MEASURED: that returns ONE PER STORE today — reflow2 opens one graph per store by convention, and his three graphs are three stores. The foundation does support many graphs per store (`{graph_id}\x00{type}\x00{id}`, `keys::graph_prefix`), so the enumeration is real but answers a question nobody currently has. THE USEFUL SHAPE IS THE OTHER ONE: a tool that DESCRIBES THE DESIGN AT A GIVEN PATH — graph id, label, node counts, mint stamp — without binding to it, so an agent that has walked the tree can show the user a menu. Splits cleanly along `dec:agent-navigates-content`: the agent finds the directories, reflow2 says what is in them.

⚠️ THE COMPLICATION NOBODY HAS SOLVED, and it bites (a) and the discovery tool equally: a RocksDB store held by a running server is EXCLUSIVELY LOCKED. Describing a design at a path while another session holds it needs a shared or read-only open. `--shared` exists and this repo's own `.mcp.json` does not pass it, which is separately why the stale-server export replay is needed at every release cut. Any answer here should say what happens when the store is busy rather than discovering it in the field.

NOT CHECKED: whether `design_identity` could take an optional path and answer for a store it is not bound to, which would make the discovery half a parameter rather than a new tool.
properties.name: OPEN — is a session pointed at a design by editing .mcp.json and reconnecting, or by a graph reference carried per call?
properties.rationale:
Kept as a question despite Anthony stating a preference, because the preference was expressed before the reconnect cost was named — and [BL-123] already records that the `/mcp` reconnect is the one step an autonomous agent cannot take, which is a direct argument against the option he leaned toward. Recording his lean AND the counter is what the brainstorm discipline is for; deciding it on the lean alone would be reading agreement into an answer given without the trade-off.

The default-when-one, refuse-when-several rule is written as the thing that should survive either choice, because it is the part that actually prevents the observed accident and it is independent of the mechanism.

The locking complication is stated because it is the kind of constraint that turns a small tool into a medium one, and it is already known to this project from a different direction.
